title: Unified Launcher starterkit for polyglot SDKs: resilient streaming, retries, and CLI scaffolder
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Deliver a compact, opinionated starterkit that scaffolds Next.js, FastAPI, and Go HTTP server examples plus a CLI generator. Focus areas: ergonomic streaming API patterns, robust retry strategies (idempotency, backoff, idempotent tokens), tokenized examples for cost-conscious batching, and ready-to-run repo templates that demonstrate production-grade telemetry and error handling. The starterkit should include: a) minimal app templates with working Redwood SDK integrations for Python, TypeScript, and Go; b) README-driven quickstart for each template; c) a CLI command to create a new sample app (redwood-launch create) with feature flags for streaming vs batch; d) cookbook snippets for common patterns (stream-to-state loops, graceful reconnects, safe retries around non-idempotent calls).
acceptance_criteria: Three runnable templates (Next.js, FastAPI, Go HTTP) checked into examples/ with README and Dockerfile
A small CLI generator (TS) that can scaffold chosen template and toggle streaming/retry modes
Example integration tests that verify streaming responses and retry behavior in CI (mocked runtime)
Doc pages that explain streaming ergonomics and recommended retry recipes with diagrams
Telemetry hooks (console traces + exported example span names) present in each template
technical_notes: JS/TS template uses fetch streaming + async iterator wrapper to demonstrate chunk parsing and backpressure handling
Python FastAPI sample shows background tasks to drain a stream and integrate with KV cache hints
Go HTTP example uses net/http with context cancellation propagation and an adapter that exposes a channel-based stream consumer
Retry strategy: idempotency token header example + configurable exponential backoff with jitter; demonstration of when not to retry (5xx vs 4xx semantics)
CLI implemented in TypeScript (node) with in-repo templates and simple flags: --stream | --batch, --quantize, --example-llm
